title: Grateful Dead Live at Gaelic Park on 1971-08-26
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude Professional 8.01 ->
source: SBD -> Master Reel (7in @ 7.5ips 1/2 Track) -> DCassette (Tascam 122mkII) -> Dat (48k) D

ai_review.summary: High‑energy August 1971 Bronx show featuring a smoking Hard to Handle and an unforgettable Empty Pages, captured on a solid patched soundboard mix.
ai_review.review: The August 26, 1971 Gaelic Park concert is widely praised for its fiery first set – highlighted by Hard to Handle, Mr. Charlie and Pigpen’s organ work – and a second‑set that rolls through classic jams like The Other One, Saint Stephen > Not Fade Away > Goin’ Down the Road.  The Charlie Miller‑Rolfe SBD has been patched, leveled and generally described as clear with only minor hiss or tape‑warble, making the performance very listenable.

ai_rating.rationale: Average fan rating ≈ 4.4 stars; most reviewers highlight strong musical moments and a good‑quality soundboard source, with only occasional minor tape hiss noted.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Patched/leveled SBD from Charlie Miller; generally clear and balanced.  Listeners note a faint hiss that fades after CD burning and occasional tape‑warble, but no major dropouts.

standout_songs: Saint Stephen > Not Fade Away > Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad
poor_songs: Beat It On Down the Line-6 (average)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Tight, song‑by‑song flow with a strong Pigpen‑centric first set and a jam‑heavy second set that builds to a memorable Saint Stephen/Not Fade Away sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: String broke during Rider; guitar briefly muted but otherwise solid playing and characteristic snarl.
band_member_comments.Phil: Stepped up for lead‑bass work on Rider, delivering a notable solo (“Sun Don't Shine”) in classic Phil fashion.
band_member_comments.Bob: Handled the vocal “headlight” part of Rider after Jerry’s string break and backed Pigpen on organ‑driven numbers.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drummers (Bill/Kreutzmann) generally strong; brief drum segment noted, occasional raggedness attributed to venue acoustics.
